risks.risk: The TV may not be 65 inches as claimed.
risks.proof: A photo showing the TV next to a known-sized object (e.g., a ruler, standard box, or a person for scale) or a close-up of the model label that includes screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a smaller screen size (e.g., 55-inch) or as unverified size, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The TV may not be 4K resolution.
risks.proof: A close-up of the model label or a screen test showing 4K content with visible resolution details (e.g., pixel density, sharpness test).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as HD or Full HD, which significantly reduces value.

risks.risk: The TV may be a refurbished or used unit, not a 2024/25 edition.
risks.proof: A photo of the original box with model and year, or a serial number check via LG’s website, or a clear shot of the model label on the back of the TV.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used or older model, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The TV may have physical damage or defects not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A 360-degree video or multiple photos showing the back, sides, stand, and screen edges for scratches, dents, or dead pixels.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially damaged, which reduces value.
